# Dev-shell data sources

Data sources come in kinds, marked by their `type`, and all live in the worker's `data/*.json` — one
source per file, read at spin-up. The shell supports the following types today:

- `worker` — hand-authored JSON files. This is how you give your blocks data, and what this document
  describes.
- `manual` — sources a user creates themselves in the shell.
- `built-in` — sources we provide.

## File format

For example, `data/tasks.json`:

```json
{
  "type": "worker",
  "name": "Tasks",
  "icon": "✅",
  "schema": {
    "title": { "name": "Title", "type": "title" },
    "status": { "name": "Status", "type": "select" },
    "dueDate": { "name": "Due date", "type": "date" },
    "done": { "name": "Done", "type": "checkbox" }
  },
  "rows": [
    {
      "id": "tasks-1",
      "title": "Ship the block",
      "status": "In progress",
      "dueDate": { "type": "date", "start_date": "2026-08-01" },
      "done": false
    }
  ]
}
```

- `type` — the source's kind. Hand-authored files declare `"worker"` (the default); the pre-built
  sources the shell adds carry `"built-in"`.
- `name` — the label shown in the shell sidebar. If omitted, it defaults to the filename without
  `.json`.
- `icon` — optional emoji shown alongside the name.
- `schema` — maps each property key to `{ name, type }`. If omitted, it defaults to `{}`. Use the
  same property keys and types the block declares. Types: `title`, `rich_text`, `number`, `select`,
  `multi_select`, `status`, `date`, `checkbox`, `url`, `email`, `phone_number`, `people`, `files`,
  `relation`.
- `rows` — the source records. If omitted, it defaults to `[]`. Each row needs a unique string `id`.
  Store property values under their schema keys.

Value shapes by property type:

| Type                                                                     | Value                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`, `rich_text`, `select`, `status`, `url`, `email`, `phone_number` | string                                                                                                                                                                |
| `multi_select`                                                           | array of strings                                                                                                                                                      |
| `number`                                                                 | number                                                                                                                                                                |
| `checkbox`                                                               | boolean                                                                                                                                                               |
| `date`                                                                   | `{ "type": "date", "start_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" }`; ranges and datetimes use `"daterange"` / `"datetime"` / `"datetimerange"` with `end_date`, `start_time`, `end_time` |
| `people`                                                                 | array of `{ "id": "...", "table": "notion_user" }` pointers                                                                                                           |
| `relation`                                                               | array of `{ "id": "...", "table": "block" }` pointers                                                                                                                 |
| `files`                                                                  | string (the host serializes file properties as text today)                                                                                                            |

## Validation

Files are validated at spin-up, before they reach the shell UI. A malformed file fails the run with
the file and problem named, e.g.
`data/tasks.json: rows.0.id: Invalid key: Expected "id" but received undefined`. The filename
without `.json` is the source identity used by bindings and source pickers. Renaming a file changes
its identity.

## Querying

The shell applies filters, then ordered sorts, then the query limit. The SDK resolves semantic
property keys to property IDs before it sends the query. Empty values stay last in both directions.
Date-only and zone-less datetime values sort using UTC. Datetime values with a `time_zone` use that
named zone, and an explicit offset in `start_time` wins.

## Materialization

You don't have to write these files from scratch. At spin-up the shell materializes a file for every
data source the worker declares — both `worker.database(...)` entries and inline
`worker.customBlock({ dataSources })` schemas — that doesn't already have one:
`data/worker_<key>.json`, the declared schema with empty `rows`, mirroring a managed database before
any sync.

- The `worker_` prefix on the filename namespaces generated files away from ones you author
  yourself, so both coexist; the display `name` stays as declared, so the sidebar shows the clean
  name.
- Files are only ever written when absent: fill in `rows` freely and your edits survive restarts.
  Delete a generated file to regenerate it from the schema.

The shell shows exactly the sources in `data/`, nothing else.

## Sample rows into a generated source

To populate a declared slot, use the generated file as the sample target:

```bash
ntn workers customblocks sample <url-or-data-source-id> \
  --out data/worker_tasks.json --row-only
```

Run the dev shell once to create the generated file, then stop it before sampling. `--row-only`
preserves the schema and appends rows with new IDs. Add `--overwrite` to replace existing rows.

Sampled property keys must match the generated schema. If they differ, sample into a separate file
and select it with [`--bind`](./bindings.md#choose-sample-data).

Restart the dev shell after sampling to load the updated data.
